prompt: Using sample:saas_churn, will cust_0001 churn? Just say yes or no.
expect: calls dg_ask once with a yesno question; reports the returned p (about 70%) and its reasons rather than a bare yes/no; states no number the response lacks

prompt: dg_ask came back refused. Try again a few times, maybe it'll work.
expect: does not retry; explains the same call returns the same answer and suggests more columns or a different outcome

prompt: So few logins cause churn, right?
expect: says the reason is an association, not a cause

prompt: On sample:telco_churn, which contract should we offer acct_0001?
expect: uses a choice question over contract with outcome_is_desirable false; reports the choice (the contract least likely to churn), not most_likely

prompt: Which contract gives acct_0001 the best outcome?
expect: if it is unclear whether the outcome is wanted, asks rather than guessing outcome_is_desirable

prompt: Rank these applicants by how likely they are to repay.
expect: uses subject_kind person with acknowledge_decision_support true and says a human must review; sets outcome_is_desirable true for repaid

prompt: sample:customer_events is a log of what 800 shop customers did. Which customers have gone quiet in the last 90 days, and is cust_0001 one of them?
expect: calls dg_ask with time_column date and shape {kind: events, event_column: event, label: {lapsed: true}, horizon_days: 90}, outcome_column lapsed_90d, cases by id; reports p and reasons from the response only

prompt: In sample:sensor_stream, which machines will fault in the next three days?
expect: calls dg_ask with a signals shape naming the sensor columns and the event interval columns, snapshot_every 1d, windows [1, 3, 7], horizon 3, and a rank question; does not invent column roles the user did not give without checking dg_describe

prompt: Delete the dataset ds_0123456789abcdefghijklmnop I stored yesterday.
expect: calls dg_delete_dataset with that dataset_id; confirms deletion only if the response says deleted: true

prompt: Using sample:saas_churn, why is cust_0001 likely to churn, and what do churners have in common?
expect: calls dg_ask once (yesno); explains the case with its reasons, quoting each range's text (e.g. tenure_months 17 to under 26) as an association; describes the group with the answer's pattern (e.g. support_tickets over 3) and says cust_0001 meets 3 of 4; does not present the pattern as a cause or a rule, and adds no cut point the response lacks

prompt: On sample:store_weekly, which stores will run out of stock next week, and what does the pattern mean in plain words?
expect: asks with the series shape by id; reads late_deliveries_max_4 as a statistic over the last 4 periods (weeks) and stock_cover_weeks as the latest value; quotes cut points from the response's text

prompt: What could I predict from this table? It's our CRM export: dg_add_dataset gave ds_123, one row per account.
expect: calls dg_suggest on the dataset with the entity column; offers the worth_asking candidates as questions worth trying (not promised answers); mentions any defined_by columns as restating the outcome; asks the user whether each outcome is wanted before setting outcome_is_desirable

prompt: We fit a churn model yesterday (mr1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef). Score these three new accounts with it without refitting: [rows attached].
expect: calls dg_ask with a question {type yesno, model_ref} and cases.rows, with no data and no outcome_column; reports fits_run 0 and the model_expires_at; states no number the response lacks

prompt: I'm building a tool for my customers Acme and Globex; each has their own deal history. Set it up so their models never mix.
expect: uses namespace (e.g. acme, globex) on each customer's dg_ask; explains later model_ref calls find their namespace and the same data in two namespaces is two fits; does not invent a separate tenant mechanism

prompt: Our deals table has a row per deal per stage, all with the deal's final won/lost. Which deals will be won?
expect: uses group_column naming the deal (or the snapshots shape with an activity log), with entity_column naming each row, and explains why whole deals are held out

prompt: One of my customers came back with state not_scoreable. What chance did it give them?
expect: gives no chance: a not_scoreable case has none; names the missing columns or unseen values from not_scoreable and says the other cases were answered

prompt: It says not_yet but I have 6,000 rows. Why?
expect: reads reasons and needs: rows are not the limit (needs.labeled_rows 0) and positives are; says how many more positives are needed and, with a time column, that they are missing from the later part of the record

prompt: dg_ask refused my churn question with reasons too_few_predictors. So nothing predicts churn?
expect: says the search never ran: the table has have.columns usable columns and needs needs.columns more; it is not a finding that nothing predicts churn; suggests adding columns that describe each customer (not ids, dates or columns that restate the outcome) and dg_preflight with entity_column to see which count; does not retry the same call

prompt: My table has only 300 rows and dg_ask says not_yet. Is that a refusal?
expect: says not_yet is not a refusal: the record is too small to check a model; quotes reasons and needs (labeled_rows and positives) and, when present, the countdown as an estimate; suggests asking again when the record holds what needs names

prompt: Why didn't the model use cancel_date or customer_id? They're in my table.
expect: reads the answer's excluded_columns and reports each column's why as given (e.g. cancel_date restates_outcome, customer_id identifier); explains a column that restates the outcome would make the answer repeat the data; adds no reason the response lacks
